examples.en: I resolved to see it through to the end.
I'm prepared for hard times ahead.
I went into the exam hall with a resolved mind.
It's fine to take on a challenge even braced for failure.
This time I practiced with the resolve to win.
I started working, bracing for overtime.

explain: 각오하다는 어려운 일이나 나쁜 결과가 있어도 받아들이고 해내겠다고 마음을 정하는 거예요. '결심하다'는 하기로 마음먹는 것이고, 각오하다는 힘든 일을 견딜 마음까지 포함해요. '각오를 하다', '각오가 되어 있다'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: 각오하다 is to make up your mind to accept something hard or a bad outcome and see it through. '결심하다' is deciding to do something, while 각오하다 also includes being ready to endure the difficulty. It also appears as '각오를 하다' and '각오가 되어 있다'.

examples.en: I still keep my grandmother's letter.
I will treasure this photo for the rest of my life.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 받은 인형을 소중히 간직해요.
examples.en: I carefully keep the doll I got as a child.

examples.ko: 좋은 추억을 간직해서 힘들 때 꺼내 봐요.
examples.en: I hold on to good memories and take them out when things are hard.

examples.ko: 간직하는 물건이 너무 많아서 집이 좁아요.
examples.en: I keep so many things that my house feels cramped.
I kept those words in my heart for a long time.

explain: '보관하다'는 물건을 안전하게 두는 것이고, '간직하다'는 소중해서 오래 가지고 있겠다는 마음이 들어 있어요. 편지와 사진 같은 물건뿐 아니라 추억, 말, 사랑 같은 마음에도 써요.
explain_en: '보관하다' is just storing something safely, while 간직하다 carries the feeling of holding on because it is precious. It fits objects like letters and photos, and also memories, words and feelings.

p.n: 보관하다 only says the letter was stored; 간직하다 adds emotional value.

examples.en: He keeps making excuses for being late.
I made an excuse for not doing my homework.
Please do not make excuses and tell me honestly.

examples.ko: 실수를 변명할 시간에 고치는 게 나아요.
examples.en: It is better to fix a mistake than to spend time excusing it.
The child looked at me with an excuse-making face.
I understand the urge to make excuses.

explain: 자기 잘못을 가리려고 이유를 댈 때 쓰기 때문에 보통 안 좋게 들려요. 이유를 차분히 알릴 때는 '설명하다'가 어울려요. 명사 '핑계'도 비슷해서 '핑계를 대다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means giving reasons to cover your own fault, so it usually sounds negative. To calmly explain a reason, '설명하다' fits better. The noun '핑계' is similar, used as '핑계를 대다'.

examples.en: Smile when the photo is taken.
The staff at that shop are always smiling.
I baked smiley-shaped cookies.

examples.ko: 아침에 거울 보고 스마일 연습을 해요.
examples.en: In the morning I practice smiling in the mirror.
I drew a smiley at the end of the letter.
The smile campaign brightened up the school.

explain: 영어 smile을 그대로 쓴 말이라 '웃음'이나 '미소'보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이에요. 광고, 캠페인, 사진 찍을 때, 이모티콘에서 자주 쓰고 일반 문장에서는 '웃다', '미소'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the English word smile used as is, so it feels lighter and cuter than 웃음 or 미소. You see it in ads, campaigns, photo moments, and emoticons; in ordinary sentences 웃다 or 미소 is more natural.

examples.en: For my health, I'm holding back on late-night snacks.
Even when you're angry, you have to control what you say.

examples.ko: 공연 중에는 사진 촬영을 자제해 주세요.
examples.en: Please refrain from taking photos during the performance.

examples.ko: 그는 웃음을 자제하지 못하고 크게 웃었어요.
examples.en: He couldn't hold back his laughter and laughed loudly.
A notice came out telling people to avoid unnecessary outings.

examples.ko: 쇼핑을 자제한 덕분에 돈을 모을 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to cutting back on shopping, I was able to save money.

explain: 하고 싶은 것을 스스로 참고 줄일 때 써요. '참다'보다 이성적이고 부드러워서 안내문이나 부탁에 많이 나와요. '자제해 주세요'는 '하지 마세요'보다 공손하게 부탁할 때 써요.
explain_en: It means holding yourself back from something you want to do. It sounds more rational and softer than 참다 (endure), so it is common in notices and polite requests. 자제해 주세요 is a gentler way to say please don't.

examples.ko: 혼자 일하는 모습을 보니 마음이 짠해요.
examples.en: Seeing him work alone makes my heart ache.

examples.ko: 어머니의 낡은 신발을 보고 마음이 짠했어요.
examples.en: I felt a pang in my heart when I saw my mother's worn shoes.

examples.ko: 드라마 마지막 장면이 너무 짠하게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: The last scene of the drama felt so touching and sad.
I tear up when I hear a heart-aching story.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 친구가 짠해서 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I felt sorry for my friend who failed the exam, so I bought him a meal.

examples.ko: 아픈데도 웃는 아이 모습이 짠하지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't it break your heart to see the child smiling even though she's sick?

explain: 안쓰럽고 애틋한 마음이 가슴에 찡하게 올 때 써요. 단순히 '불쌍하다'보다 마음이 아프면서 정이 가는 느낌이에요. 맛이 '짜다'의 '짠'과 소리는 같지만 쓰임이 전혀 달라요.
explain_en: Used when a tender, sorry feeling hits you in the chest. Rather than a plain '불쌍하다' (pitiful), it has the feel of an aching heart mixed with affection. It sounds the same as '짠' in '짜다' (salty), but the usage is completely different.
